title: Part Three: The 1929 Deal, Then and Now

sections.brief: What the Treaty, Concordat and Financial Convention gave the Holy See and Mussolini's Italy, article by article; Pius XI's 13 February 1929 allocution; the 1931 Catholic Action crisis as evidence that the deal was a bargain, not a merger. Figures: fig-compare

Constitution Art. 7; the Villa Madama Agreement of 18 February 1984 (Craxi-Casaroli), Law 121/1985, the end of the state religion, optional religious teaching, the end of the oath and the congrua; Law 222/1985 on Church bodies and clergy pay. Figures: fig-compare (1929 vs 1984)

How 0.8% of IRPEF is allocated, including unexpressed choices; MEF figures for tax years 2021 and 2022; the CEI's 2026 allocation and clergy pay; the Corte dei conti critique and the CEI reply. Figures: fig-money, fig-flow

The ICI exemption for non-commercial entities; Commission decision of 19 December 2012; General Court 2016; CJEU 6 November 2018 (C-622/16 P to C-624/16 P); Commission recovery decision of 3 March 2023; Italy's recovery procedure and its status as of October 2026; who benefits today and what it costs.
